name: OWASP Top 10 CI/CD Security Risks
source_notes: Verified against the OWASP project page and its per-risk pages, plus the project repo index.md; GitHub Actions hardening signals from GitHub's own security-hardening docs.
caveats: Only edition is v1.0 (2022, described as September-October 2022 by a summarizing fetch); no 2024-2026 update found. Effectively unmaintained but still canonical.
Maturity is uncertain: repo front-matter shows only level: 3 (Lab per the inferred mapping); a summary also described it as "Lab/Incubator".
Authors Daniel Krivelevich and Omer Gil (Cider Security); Cider's later acquisition is unverified.
The notes attribute no CWEs to these items.
GitHub Actions detection signals come from GitHub's hardening guide and reinhardt inference, not OWASP text.

items.name: Insufficient Flow Control Mechanisms
items.summary: An attacker with access to one CI/CD system can push malicious code or artifacts down the pipeline alone because no additional approval or review is enforced.
prevention: Protect branches without exclusions.
Limit auto-merge rules.
Require approval for production pipelines.
Accept only artifacts from pre-approved CI service accounts.
Detect configuration drift.

static: Auto-merge workflows (gh pr merge --auto, unconditional Dependabot auto-merge)
Deploy on push to any branch (branches: ["**"]) with production secrets
review: Branch protection and required-review settings in the SCM

items.name: Inadequate Identity and Access Management
items.summary: Identities across CI/CD systems are poorly managed: stale, overprivileged, shared or unmanaged accounts.
prevention: Continuously map identities and remove unneeded permissions.
Disable stale accounts and use a central IdP.
Give external collaborators expiring access; no personal emails or self-registration.
Avoid broad base permissions and shared accounts.

static: permissions: write-all or no top-level permissions key in workflows
contents: write / id-token: write on PR-triggered jobs
review: SCM and CI user and permission inventory

items.name: Dependency Chain Abuse
items.summary: A malicious package is fetched and executed by the build, through dependency confusion, typosquatting and similar techniques.
prevention: Pull packages through an internal proxy.
Verify checksums and signatures.
Do not configure clients to pull the latest version.
Register private packages under the organization scope and commit .npmrc.
Isolate install scripts from secrets and do not publish internal project names.

static: npm install without a lockfile or with --no-package-lock; no npm ci
Docker FROM image:latest or no digest
Unscoped internal package names
curl | bash in steps

items.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution (PPE)
items.summary: Attackers run malicious commands in a pipeline by modifying its config (direct PPE), files it invokes (indirect PPE), or via anonymous PRs on public repos (public PPE).
prevention: Run unreviewed code on isolated nodes without access to secrets.
Require manual approval for pipelines triggered by fork PRs.
Align branch protection with pipeline triggers.
Review CI configuration changes.
Grant pipeline credentials least privilege.

static: pull_request_target or workflow_run with actions/checkout of head.sha/head.ref followed by run steps
${{ github.event.(issue|pull_request|comment|review|head_commit).* }} or github.head_ref interpolated in run:
self-hosted runners on public repos
review: Which files the pipeline executes and who can change them

items.name: Insufficient PBAC (Pipeline-Based Access Controls)
items.summary: Pipeline execution nodes and steps get more access to secrets, systems and network than they need.
prevention: Do not share nodes across sensitivity levels.
Scope secrets per pipeline and step.
Revert nodes to a pristine state after runs.
Run with a least-privilege OS user.
Restrict network and internet egress.

static: permissions: write-all
secrets: inherit to reusable workflows
Job-wide secrets where a single step needs them

items.name: Insufficient Credential Hygiene
items.summary: Credentials used across CI/CD are static, shared, over-scoped or leaked into code, logs and artifacts.
prevention: Map credentials and do not share them across contexts.
Prefer temporary over static credentials and scope them to IP or identity.
Detect secrets in the IDE, on push and in history.
Prevent secrets printing to console.
Verify secrets are removed from artifacts such as image layers, binaries and Helm charts.

static: Literal secrets in workflow env: instead of ${{ secrets.X }}
echo ${{ secrets.X }}
ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
Long-lived AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID secrets instead of OIDC role-to-assume
Dockerfile ENV/ARG with secret-like literals

items.name: Insecure System Configuration
items.summary: CI/CD systems (SCM, CI servers, registries) run with insecure settings, outdated versions or excessive access.
prevention: Inventory and patch CI/CD systems.
Restrict network access to the minimum.
Review configuration periodically.
Apply least privilege on execution nodes and be careful with debug access.

static: ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG or set -x alongside secrets (weak signal)
review: SCM/CI server configuration, mostly outside the repo

items.name: Ungoverned Usage of 3rd Party Services
items.summary: Third-party services connected to CI/CD (marketplace apps, plugins, OAuth apps, PATs) are adopted and granted access without governance.
prevention: Require approval before integrating third parties.
Maintain visibility of permissions granted versus used.
Deprovision unused integrations.
Run third parties in the build with limited access to secrets and code and strict ingress/egress filters.

static: Third-party actions given broad tokens or secrets
review: Installed apps and OAuth grants in the SCM

items.name: Improper Artifact Integrity Validation
items.summary: Code and artifacts can be tampered with along the pipeline because their integrity is not validated.
prevention: Sign code and artifacts.
Verify artifacts with tools such as in-toto, SLSA and Sigstore.
Detect configuration drift.
Check hashes of third-party scripts fetched in the build against official published hashes.

static: uses: owner/action@main, @master, mutable tags (e.g. @v1) or no ref instead of a full commit SHA
curl | sh / ADD http... without hash verification
Docker images without digest pinning
review: Signing and verification in release flows

items.name: Insufficient Logging and Visibility
items.summary: CI/CD activity is not logged or monitored well enough to detect or investigate attacks.
prevention: Map the environment and enable logging, which is often off by default.
Ship logs to a SIEM.
Alert on anomalies.

review: Audit log configuration and alerting for SCM and CI
